question: Can activation statistics align independently trained sparse-autoencoder features across adjacent transformer layers well enough to visualize feature persistence, emergence, specialization, and composition?

key_findings.claim: The paper constructs a large cross-layer feature graph from four complementary activation-similarity measures and releases an interactive browser for exploring it.
key_findings.evidence: For each of GPT-2 small's 11 adjacent residual-stream layer pairs, every one of 24,576 res-jb SAE features is paired with every next-layer feature. Pearson correlation uses magnitudes; Jaccard uses thresholded co-activation; sufficiency estimates downstream-given-upstream firing; and necessity estimates upstream-given-downstream firing, producing roughly six billion candidate edges per layer pair.

anchors.section: Appendix A-B, computation pipeline and relative thresholds
Appendix D, distribution of similarity values

key_findings.claim: Very high adjacent-layer Pearson correlation identifies convincing examples of persistent features, but most dictionary entries do not meet the paper's pass-through criterion.
key_findings.evidence: At the subjectively calibrated threshold of Pearson at least 0.95, the paper traces a panic/fear feature through layers 0 to 5 with correlations from 0.96 to 0.99. Figure 3 simultaneously indicates that more than half of features at each layer, rising toward 80 percent in later layers, are classified as appearing or disappearing rather than passed through.

anchors.section: 3.1 Features being passed through multiple layers
Appendix G, pass-through features at different thresholds

key_findings.claim: The reported AND and OR motifs are one-way conditional associations, not demonstrated logic gates.
key_findings.evidence: High necessity for two upstream features only shows that a downstream activation usually co-occurs with both; it does not show that their conjunction is sufficient to produce it. High sufficiency for either input only shows each tends to accompany the downstream feature; it does not show the downstream activates only from their disjunction. The examples are manually interpreted from binarized co-activations and receive no joint-intervention truth table.

key_findings.claim: Correlation scores are at best weak causal-screening signals in the paper's own ablation study.
key_findings.evidence: The authors explicitly frame the graph as correlational. Their reconstruction-error-preserving single-feature ablations show increasing median absolute downstream change across similarity bins, but no effect-size correlation, uncertainty estimate, sign, task-level outcome, or matched random-control result is reported. Redundant causes are acknowledged to be missed.

anchors.section: Establishing causality between features through ablation

key_findings.claim: Projecting next-layer SAE reconstruction error onto a previous-layer decoder vector does not establish that a disappearing concept has left the residual stream.
key_findings.evidence: The analysis looks for a linear component of the next-layer residual error along the old feature direction and reports no evidence of recovery. A concept can rotate, split across several features, be represented nonlinearly, or cancel in that one projection; moreover a transformer block intervenes between the two residual streams. The conclusion that the features no longer exist downstream is therefore stronger than the diagnostic supports.

anchors.section: 3.3 Did features disappear, or did they lack representation

key_findings.claim: Community detection produces plausible semantic chains and specialization examples, but evidence is qualitative and depends heavily on graph and labeling choices.
key_findings.evidence: Leiden and Louvain communities show examples such as a broad evidence feature specializing to court evidence and a special-related feature specializing to law-enforcement titles. No annotated gold standard, held-out clustering metric, stability analysis, or comparison across graph constructions quantifies semantic validity, while the authors note many graph hyperparameters and inaccurate GPT-3.5 labels.

key_findings.claim: The empirical scope is too narrow to separate transformer feature evolution from one SAE family's training artifacts.
key_findings.evidence: All main conclusions use one 124M-parameter model, one res-jb residual-stream SAE suite, one corpus, relative thresholds set from corpus maxima, and mostly GPT-3.5 summaries. Later evidence across six models and three SAE families shows that even unambiguous single-token features have materially different cross-layer persistence and causal redundancy depending on the SAE recipe.

method.core_idea: Treat independently trained per-layer SAE dictionaries as nodes in a multipartite graph and connect adjacent-layer features when their activations have similar statistical patterns over a large corpus.
method.mechanism: The pipeline passes Pile tokens through GPT-2 small and each layer's residual-stream SAE, accumulates pairwise Pearson and thresholded co-activation statistics in batches, removes edges below 0.1, visualizes prompt-active or community-selected subgraphs, and applies Leiden or Louvain clustering. High Pearson links identify pass-through chains; asymmetric conditional probabilities suggest compositions; selected zero ablations and reconstruction-error projections probe causality and missing downstream representation.
assumptions: Independently trained SAE features with similar corpus activation patterns represent the same or closely related model feature.
Normalizing each latent by its observed maximum and binarizing at 20 percent yields comparable active/inactive events across features.
Corpus-level adjacent-layer co-activation captures reusable computation rather than shared input causes or SAE artifacts.
GPT-3.5 descriptions and top activating tokens are adequate semantic evidence for evaluating discovered links and communities.
A previous-layer decoder direction remains a meaningful probe direction in the next layer's residual space.

techniques.role: Represents layer-specific SAE latents as nodes and activation similarity as directed inter-layer edges.
Accumulates counts, sums, and squares without caching trillions of activation values.
Defines firing relative to each feature's corpus maximum before Jaccard and conditional-probability calculations.
Extracts multi-layer subgraphs of densely connected, putatively related features.
Zeros one SAE latent while adding the original SAE reconstruction residual back before measuring downstream activations.
Tests whether a missing aligned feature remains in the next SAE's reconstruction error along its former decoder direction.

evaluations.setting: GPT-2 small with 12 res-jb residual-stream SAEs over 10 million Pile tokens
evaluations.metric: All-pairs adjacent-layer Pearson, Jaccard, necessity, and sufficiency
evaluations.result: The pipeline creates four 11-by-24,576-by-24,576 similarity tensors and thresholds values below 0.1 for downstream use.
evaluations.baseline: No alternate model, SAE seed, architecture, corpus, or independently trained dictionary suite.

evaluations.metric: Fraction with at least one high-correlation neighbor and qualitative semantic agreement
evaluations.result: Some features persist over many layers, including a six-layer panic chain, while a majority of entries per layer appear or disappear under the selected threshold.
evaluations.baseline: Threshold is calibrated by one interactive manual binary search over GPT-3.5 descriptions; no assignment or data-free matching baseline.

evaluations.metric: NaN-pattern overlap and mean absolute Pearson difference between 10M and 100M tokens
evaluations.result: The paper reports 97.7 percent overlap in missing entries and mean absolute difference 0.00019 for corresponding values, motivating 10M-token computation.
evaluations.baseline: Global matrix agreement; no stability analysis limited to selected high-score edges, rare features, communities, or threshold crossings.

evaluations.setting: Selected inter-layer feature ablations across 10 similarity bins and 11 layer pairs
evaluations.metric: Absolute mean change in downstream latent activation
evaluations.result: Higher similarity bins generally show larger effects for all four measures, with Jaccard weakest; results are shown as boxplots.
evaluations.baseline: No random-feature, activation-magnitude-matched, task-faithfulness, multi-feature, or false-discovery-controlled baseline.

evaluations.setting: Leiden and Louvain communities plus conditional-probability motifs
evaluations.metric: Manual semantic coherence of GPT-3.5 descriptions and top activations
evaluations.result: The paper exhibits pass-through chains, apparent specialization, approximate AND/OR motifs, and several label errors exposed by high-correlation neighbors.
evaluations.baseline: Illustrative case studies only, without blinded raters, a semantic gold standard, clustering stability, or formal gate interventions.

limitations: Author-stated: similarity graphs are correlational, and the ablations only weakly associate the proposed scores with causal effects.
Author-stated: sparse co-activation leaves many pairs supported by fewer than ten samples even at ten million tokens.
Author-stated: activation, edge, and community-detection hyperparameters materially shape the graph, and only four similarity measures are developed.
Author-stated: semantic analysis mostly trusts GPT-3.5 summaries that the authors themselves find can be inaccurate.
Reviewer inference: maximum-relative thresholding is outlier-sensitive and uses a corpus-dependent scale, so edge identities may change under domain or sample-size shift.
Reviewer inference: one GPT-2-small SAE family cannot establish that motifs persist under SAE seeds, widths, objectives, activation functions, or larger models.
Reviewer inference: neither logic-gate nor disappearance claims receive the necessary joint causal interventions or representation-complete tests.
failure_modes: Two features driven by the same token or context can correlate across layers without one transmitting or computing the other.
Independent SAE dictionaries can split, merge, duplicate, or rotate one underlying representation, producing apparent births, deaths, and specialization artifacts.
A single extreme activation inflates a feature's maximum and suppresses its binary firing rate under the 20-percent rule.
High conditional probabilities from rare co-activations can create spurious AND/OR-looking motifs.
Single-feature ablation misses redundant causes and can induce off-manifold states; absolute downstream changes also confound latent scale.
Generic modularity optimization can group high-degree or threshold artifacts into communities that appear coherent after selective manual labeling.
reusable_insights: Use several asymmetric and symmetric similarity measures because persistence, implication, and co-activation are distinct hypotheses.
Preserve SAE reconstruction error during latent ablations to avoid attributing the whole reconstruction gap to one feature.
Treat correlational feature-flow graphs as candidate generators and require task-linked interventions before calling an edge causal.
Match or jointly train cross-layer dictionaries across multiple SAE seeds and families before interpreting feature birth, death, or specialization.
Test proposed Boolean composition with complete intervention truth tables over inputs and their combinations.
open_questions: Which cross-layer matches are stable across SAE families, random seeds, dictionary widths, corpora, and model scales?
Can optimal transport, data-free folded-weight matching, or a jointly trained cross-layer SAE distinguish persistence from independently rediscovered semantics?
Do causally validated feature-flow communities predict model outputs or enable precise steering better than prompt-specific sparse feature circuits?
How can split, merge, redundancy, and nonlinear composition be represented without forcing a one-feature-to-one-feature graph?
What formal tests distinguish an actual Boolean computation from high conditional co-activation?

competitive_landscape.title: Sparse Feature Circuits: Discovering and Editing Interpretable Causal Graphs in Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Marks et al. build prompt- and behavior-specific feature circuits with attribution and interventions, including editing applications; the reviewed work trades causal/task specificity for a cheap corpus-wide graph over every adjacent-layer feature pair.

competitive_landscape.title: Transcoders Find Interpretable LLM Feature Circuits
competitive_landscape.difference: Dunefsky et al. train transcoders to sparsify the MLP input-output map and derive weight-based feature circuits on models up to 1.4B parameters; the reviewed method links separate residual SAEs statistically and therefore cannot directly resolve nonlinear sublayer computation.

competitive_landscape.title: Mechanistic Permutability: Match Features Across Layers
competitive_landscape.difference: SAE Match appeared two days earlier on arXiv and aligns layer dictionaries without activation data by folding thresholds into SAE parameters, evaluated on Gemma 2; the reviewed paper uses corpus co-activation, richer graph motifs, GPT-2 small, and partial causal checks.

competitive_landscape.title: Analyze Feature Flow to Enhance Interpretation and Steering in Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Laptev et al. explicitly extend earlier inter-layer feature links using data-free cosine maps and validate their utility through targeted feature amplification and suppression; the reviewed work stops mainly at exploratory visualization and small ablations.

competitive_landscape.title: Route Sparse Autoencoder to Interpret Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: RouteSAE learns a shared feature space from routed multi-layer activations and reports larger-scale Llama-3.2-1B interpretability and steering results; the reviewed paper post-hoc aligns independent layer dictionaries and cannot control their representational mismatch.

competitive_landscape.title: Are Single-Token Sparse Autoencoder Features Causally Necessary? Layer-Depth and SAE-Family Effects
competitive_landscape.difference: Cho et al. study 3.9 million features across six models and three SAE families, finding cross-family causal and persistence differences even for exactly matchable single-token features; this directly cautions against generalizing the reviewed graph from one res-jb suite.

competitive_landscape.title: Descriptive Collision in Sparse Autoencoder Auto-Interpretability: When One Explanation Describes Many Features
competitive_landscape.difference: McCann shows that 82.1 percent of a large human-annotated SAE set share their description with another feature and proposes discrimination metrics; the reviewed semantic validation leans on even coarser GPT-3.5 summaries and can mistake shared wording for feature identity.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: this work introduces a corpus-wide vertical SAE feature graph and browser, revealing pass-through features, apparent Boolean combinations, specialization, communities, and auto-interpretation errors. Reviewer inference after primary-source comparison: combining four all-pairs activation statistics with a usable interactive graph is a useful exploratory contribution and broader than the prompt-specific sparse-feature-circuit predecessor. Priority for cross-layer alignment is not exclusive: SAE Match appeared almost simultaneously and uses a data-free method, while transcoders already targeted causal inter-feature computation. The strongest claims should be narrowed to candidate motifs—the Boolean, disappearance, and semantic-community interpretations are not causally or quantitatively established, and later multi-model/family evidence shows the underlying SAE representation is a critical experimental variable.
reviewer_notes: Read all twenty-three extracted pages, including the complete similarity and sampling pipeline, threshold calibration, all qualitative cases, ablation algorithm and plots, error projection, community construction, and label-error appendix. I audited the direction of the conditional probabilities behind the AND/OR language, distinguished a one-direction projection from evidence of feature absence, and checked seven primary-source predecessors, simultaneous competitors, extensions, and current stress tests through August 2026.
